replies.body:
dont accept too many OCN teams - they don't bloody show up
We're not going to exclude a certain group from participating in a tournament. We're welcoming as much as we are to allow any player group, server, or team to participate and we won't take that privilege away.

Be more forgiving on small violations of the rules
Depends on the rule, always does. In general, just don't break them. I wasn't involved in the BC punishment but in general I thought we would be forgiving, at least in circumstances where it'd be minor and not really heavily apply. The only rules we really upheld strongly were the most important.

And please please don't have half the community on the same official server watching the game
Didn't witness it, but I for sure would encourage livestreamers and referees to spread out...

Have more staff organising the tourneys
We actually are fine with how we are now, we had a larger team but it made things worse. Remember when we had the tournament committee and did nothing an entire year? It's better we cut down and found more efficiency and power in doing this.

Improve the general organisation
Internally, it was fine for the most part, but I'd like for more communication and less last-minute decisions on things. We tried to avoid disorganization as much as possible.

Make fairer groups
Sure, I guess.

replies.author: badgg
replies.body:
Here is some focus points for me, personally & the official team (in my opinion)

Organisation
There is no doubt, that the organisation of this tournament wasn't up to our expectations as such. Prime example of this was the layout of the information sub category - which was somewhat difficult to navigate around. This is certainly something we will work on for the next tournament, and we will ensure this time no one has difficulties finding what they need to find.

Decision making
After the tournament (early this morning), the officials were admitting that some of the decisions made were rushed. Although we observed and discussed particular issues carefully, we probably didn't do our best. This is something I will make sure myself, that I personally, don't rush. 

Maps
We understand that some of the maps may have not played out too well, probably because we didn't host a map testing event. (We did but only Bad Company attended (props to you guys)). Potentially - we could ensure that all teams test the maps, extensively to iron out bugs and build additions to improve the gameplay.

Referees
Improved training process is definitely something that was mentioned in the Officials chat. We should, and probably will, design a new system in that regard.

Tournament structure
In my opinion, the tournament should be within 1-2 days... not weeks/months. This allows less "no shows" and organisation within the team.

Rules
No doubt, this field will be heavily improved on. We don't want any confusion again.

replies.author: TheOpAmerican
replies.body:
Football (soccer) is a fair point system, it works throughout the world, however there are different variations of the soccer scoring system that could be used instead (such as the 10 point system)

Here it is (tweaked slightly to fit an Avicus tournament) :

1. 6 Points for each win
2. 3 Points for a tie.
3. Zero points for a loss
4. 1 extra Point for a shutout + win.
5. 1 Point for each monument broken (up to 3)
6. No shutout bonus point for a 0-0 tie.


Example:
Cacalmarin VS Randys 

Cacalmarin WINS by breaking 2 monuments vs Randys 0.

Cacalmarin gets 6 points for winning, plus 1 point for a shutout, 2 points for breaking 2 monuments, which equals 9 points. (one point was dropped in the process due to this scenario being a two-monument match, which will still be fair since teams play on the same map)
